A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimVQ research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy experiments, ImageNet and LibriTTS reconstruction results, ablations, training-dynamics analyses, and qualitative reconstruction examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds encoder/codebook distribution and code-usage frequency analyses in Figures 5 and 7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains Gaussian initialization and freezing of C, optimization of the linear basis W, nearest-neighbor quantization, straight-through estimation, and the same training objective. No proposed method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet reconstruction, LibriTTS audio reconstruction, and the same two-dimensional toy setting. The new distribution analyses reuse ImageNet validation data. Downstream generation is discussed but not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding reconstruction, ablation, and loss-curve comparisons retain their comparator sets after table renumbering. The new distribution plots use the existing vanilla VQ comparator; newly discussed related methods are not added to the reported benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises the reported latent dimensions from FSQ 16 to 6 and LFQ 6 to 16; no rerun is documented. New Figure 5 specifies visualization on a random ImageNet validation subset. Existing reconstruction splits, budgets, and metrics otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds encoder-feature/codebook alignment visualization in Figure 5 and per-code usage analysis in Appendix 8.3, Figure 7. These supplement the retained codebook-size, initialization, freezing, toy-optimization, rank, norm, and loss-curve analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new frequency plots describe code activity rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds feature/codebook distribution findings and usage-frequency profiles. Figure 7 reports 918 active codes for vanilla VQ and 65,518 for SimVQ out of 65,536. Matched reconstruction scores, ablation results, existing curves, and appendix reconstruction examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, optimization derivations, Gaussian expectation argument, convergence expressions, and memory-complexity analysis are retained. Equations are split and renumbered, without substantive mathematical additions or corrections.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims that disjoint codebook optimization causes collapse, linear-basis reparameterization addresses it, and SimVQ supports high utilization and improved reconstruction across image/audio modalities and larger codebooks. The contribution list and conclusion preserve their scientific scope.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explains that better reconstruction metrics need not produce better downstream generation and uses this distinction to delimit the evaluation focus. Section 5.4 also interprets the new distribution plots as evidence of broader feature/codebook coverage.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly defines validation-set codebook utilization in Table 1's caption and expands the unchanged Table 5 configurations into prose. However, v1's code-availability statement and repository link disappear; this removes access information without establishing that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning to cover RVQ/MoVQ, stochastic quantization, distribution penalties, and codebook resets. New Section 5.1.1 explicitly positions SimVQ as an architectural contribution and explains why those other approaches are outside its baseline selection. Section 6 adds reconstruction-versus-generation context.

P1.justification: The abstract is shortened, author and affiliation information changes, asymmetric optimization becomes a numbered subsection, and toy examples become its sub-subsection. Baseline-selection, discussion, and appendix explanatory prose are added, while most existing method and experimental narrative is retained.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column paper with separately headed supplementary material. Tables and figures are extensively resized and repositioned, table captions move below tables, and two distribution figures are added. Existing appendix reconstruction examples are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The revised FSQ/LFQ dimension entries, new distribution diagnostics, explicit utilization definition, and generation caveat improve reporting accuracy and interpretation of the evidence. The baseline rationale also makes comparison boundaries clearer. These support a modest overall improvement, tempered by removal of v1's explicit code-access link.
